excerpt_i18n.en:
Baidu's Wenku and Netdisk have officially expanded overseas. At this year's Baidu World Conference, in addition to emphasizing "internalized AI," Baidu announced the latest progress in the global rollout of several flagship products. Baidu Wenku and Netdisk are at the forefront, serving as the "vanguard" in Baidu's exploration of the global AI market.

Despite the rapid and high-profile development of foundational large models worldwide, which can create the "illusion" that AI is all-powerful, the reality is different. Overseas companies, employees, and students alike are constrained by the unhealthy "inverted pyramid" structure in the AI industry—more specific and personalized usage scenarios and needs remain largely unmet.

In China, Baidu Wenku, as a one-stop AI content acquisition and creation platform covering work, study, and even entertainment and daily life, has surpassed 90 million monthly active users, firmly leading its sector. However, overseas, products with full-modal general capabilities are rare—meaning those that integrate understanding, generation, and editing of text, images, audio, and video across the entire process, and possess abilities like task decomposition, path planning, and workflow orchestration. In short, overseas AI products are often vertical and fragmented, making all-in-one solutions like Baidu Wenku nearly impossible to find.

Particularly in regions such as the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and South America, the penetration of AI capabilities remains at levels from years ago, leaving a significant market vacuum.

Baidu Netdisk faces similar opportunities. Many overseas Chinese look forward to using it to stay connected with family and friends back home, share life experiences, leverage AI to preserve shared memories, and build an "online home" that transcends physical distance.

items.raw_excerpt: 11月15日-17日，以“AI下一个十年：场景驱动×新质引擎”为主题的2025人工智能+大会主论坛在北京中关村国际创新中心举办。大会由国家高新区人工智能产业协同创新网络、中央广播电视总台《赢在AI+》节目组、清华大学可持续社会价值研究院、中国人民大学交叉科学研究院、赛迪研究院人工智能研究中心、中关村发展集团等联合主办。由中关村科技企业家协会独家战略支持。（雷峰网）   AI顶尖智慧碰撞，共话AI下一个十年 图灵奖得主、中国科学院院士、清华大学交叉信息研究院及人工智能学院院长姚期智发表主旨演讲《人工智能的未来展望》。他提出，AI大模型正在革新各行各业，中长期要走向AGI，赋能科学，同时也必须确保AI安全、可控可靠。它的前景辽阔，影响深远，我们必须不断地创新突。中国不缺应用人才和场景，最重要的是培养更多尖端创新人才。   作为青年先锋力量的代表，宇树科技创始人兼首席执行官王兴兴以《我们的下一个十年》为题，分享了深藏心底的梦想与奔赴：我们的下⼀个十年，必将是“生长与绽放”——是机器人从“能做事”到“会做事”，从“行业工具”到“生活伙伴”的十年。 圆桌论坛环节，智谱董事长刘德兵，范式联合创始人首席科学家、执行董事陈雨强，阶跃星辰创始人兼首席执行官姜大昕，清华大学交叉信息研究院助理教授、星海图联合创始人许华哲，清华大学交叉信息研究院教授、副院长徐葳齐聚一堂围绕“生态协同，AI+未来”，从大模型、场景应用、人机未来等多方面展开前瞻对话，勾勒出人工智能技术未来发展的丰富可能性。 随后，围绕“AI规模化落地的机遇与策略”议题，清华大学计算机系副教授、面壁智能联合创始人兼首席科学家刘知远，北京数据集团副总经理、北京国际大数据交易所董事长李振军，上海交通大学特聘教授，思必驰联合创始人、首席科学家俞凯，云知声创始人兼首席执行官黄伟，阿里云智能集团副总裁霍嘉，中数睿智董事长韩涵

excerpt_i18n.en:
From November 15 to 17, 2025, the main forum of the AI+ Conference, themed "AI's Next Decade: Scenario-Driven × New Quality Engine," was held at the Beijing Zhongguancun International Innovation Center. The event was co-organized by the National High-Tech Zone AI Industry Collaborative Innovation Network, the CCTV "Win in AI+" program team, Tsinghua University's Institute for Sustainable Social Value, Renmin University of China's Institute for Interdisciplinary Sciences, CCID Think Tank's AI Research Center, and Zhongguancun Development Group, with exclusive strategic support from the Zhongguancun Technology Entrepreneurs Association. (Leifeng Network)

Top AI minds converged to discuss AI's next decade. Turing Award winner, academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Science and AI School, Yao Qizhi, delivered a keynote speech titled "Future Prospects of Artificial Intelligence." He stated that large AI models are revolutionizing various industries, with the medium to long-term goal being the advancement toward AGI to empower science, while ensuring AI is safe, controllable, and reliable. Its prospects are vast and its impact profound, necessitating continuous innovation and breakthroughs. excerpt_i18n.en:
In recent years, the AI industry has moved at an almost surreal pace. Models have repeatedly pushed boundaries, product iterations race against time, and discussions have shifted from "reasoning costs" to "emergent intelligence" and "AGI timelines," with sentiments swinging between optimism and anxiety. Amid such intense technological cycles, few pause to consider a more fundamental question: What kind of intelligence are we truly pursuing? Beyond language, are there abilities yet to be fully understood?

A week ago, Li Fei-Fei reignited this debate with a lengthy article on world models, which avoided hype or easy predictions. Its weight lay in highlighting the tough challenges current technology often sidesteps: spatial understanding, physical reasoning, embodied behavior, and real-world uncertainties—long-avoided issues laid out one by one, sparking intense discussions on world models within the AI community.

A week later, in a recent interview, Li Fei-Fei revisited the unresolved points from that article, breaking down questions she had pondered deeply but couldn't fully expand on. She provided more detailed explanations on the structural limitations of language models in world understanding, the foundational role of 3D space in intelligence formation, and the practical hurdles behind the long stagnation in robotics.

As these fragmented clues were pieced together, the interview served as a continuation and completion of the original article, offering a clearer view of the technical directions she genuinely focuses on and the logic behind them.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos años, el ritmo de la industria de la IA ha sido casi irreal. Los modelos han superado límites repetidamente, la iteración de productos parece una carrera contra el tiempo, y los debates han oscilado entre el "coste del razonamiento", la "emergencia de la inteligencia" y los "plazos para la AGI", con emociones balanceándose entre el optimismo y la ansiedad. En ciclos tecnológicos tan intensos, pocos se detienen a reflexionar sobre una cuestión más fundamental: ¿qué tipo de inteligencia estamos buscando realmente? Más allá del lenguaje, ¿existen capacidades aún no comprendidas adecuadamente? Hace una semana, Fei-Fei Li rescató este tema con un extenso artículo sobre modelos del mundo, que no exageró la revolución ni ofreció un futuro fácil, sino que destacó por señalar cómo la tecnología actual está evitando abordar aspectos clave.

excerpt_i18n.en: In the second half of 2025, two notable trends emerged in discussions within the U.S.-China AI community. First, the focus shifted from debating the generational gap in technology between the two nations to acknowledging the rise of China's AI capabilities, with some anticipating an imminent overtaking. For instance, overseas companies like Airbnb publicly stated they extensively use Tongyi Qianwen instead of frequently relying on OpenAI, while MiniMax's open-source model M2 surpassed Claude in AI coding capabilities, ranking among the top three in programming on OpenRouter. Second, both aggressive capital bets and bubble risks intensified—OpenAI signed a $1.4 trillion computing power order with suppliers like NVIDIA, and a comment from OpenAI's CFO about needing government guarantees for AI investments triggered a major sell-off in U.S. tech stocks, wiping out nearly $800 billion in market value from eight major tech giants in a week. The first trend points to the market, indicating that demand is no longer blindly pursuing peak intelligence but opting for more cost-effective, faster, and affordable Chinese models. The second trend highlights capital, revealing that the U.S. AI industry faces serious scrutiny over its high valuations and massive capital expenditures, with investors growing uneasy and panicked about the high-stakes, high-investment model requiring continuous funding for startups. Both phenomena signify that the AI narrative once dominated by U.S. tech giants like OpenAI is beginning to shift.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la segunda mitad de 2025, se observaron dos fenómenos interesantes en los círculos de IA de China y EE.UU.: primero, el enfoque dejó de ser cuántas generaciones tecnológicas separan a ambos países, para reconocer el auge de la IA china e incluso su inminente superación, como muestran empresas extranjeras como Airbnb que adoptan masivamente Tongyi Qianwen en lugar de OpenAI, o el modelo abierto MiniMax M2, cuyas capacidades de programación superan a Claude y se sitúan entre las tres primeras en OpenRouter. Segundo, las apuestas arriesgadas de capital y los riesgos de burbuja se intensificaron notablemente.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Globally, 88% of enterprises have adopted AI technologies, yet only 39% have achieved significant financial returns. This "input-output ratio" gap in AI highlights the core challenge of its industrial implementation. Intelligent agents are seen as the key wave to solve this problem, but how can they move beyond being labeled as "toys" or "concepts" to deeply integrate into industries and become productive forces that reduce costs and increase efficiency? On November 13, at the Baidu World 2025 Intelligent Agent Forum, Baidu Intelligent Cloud, in collaboration with industry and technology experts from Intel, the Key Laboratory of Big Data and AI Applications Innovation for Emergency Management, and the Digital Engineering Research Institute of China Energy Engineering Group Guangdong Institute, provided the answer: an outstanding intelligent agent must be built on a solid infrastructure. A robust Agent Infra serves as the core engine that transforms agents from "potential" into "productivity."

Building the Productivity Engine: Baidu Qianfan Agent Infra Lays a Strong Foundation

The implementation of enterprise-level agents is far from a simple "large model + prompts." Yin Dawei, General Manager of Baidu Intelligent Cloud's Platform Product Division, emphasized at the forum that intelligent agent technology has evolved over the past three years from chatbots to multimodal enterprise capabilities, requiring a unified, efficient, and scalable infrastructure to support increasingly complex development and operations. To address this, Baidu Intelligent Cloud has built a comprehensive Agent Infra centered on Baidu Qianfan, integrating agent development services, tool services, model services, and data services.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 88 % de las empresas a nivel mundial ya han implementado tecnologías de IA, pero solo el 39 % ha logrado un retorno financiero significativo. Esta brecha en la relación "inversión-resultado" de la IA revela el núcleo del desafío en la aplicación industrial de la IA. Los agentes inteligentes son considerados la clave para superar este obstáculo, pero ¿cómo pueden dejar de ser meros "juguetes" o "conceptos" y convertirse realmente en herramientas de "productividad" que reduzcan costos y mejoren la eficiencia en la industria? El 13 de noviembre, en el Foro de Agentes Inteligentes de Baidu World 2025, Baidu Intelligent Cloud, junto con Intel, el Laboratorio Clave de Gestión de Emergencias para Innovación en Aplicaciones de Big Data e IA, el Instituto de Ingeniería Digital del Grupo de Construcción Energética de China en Guangdong y otros expertos industriales y técnicos, ofrecieron la respuesta: excelencia.
